answer: The protocol calls its three gates dune (identity binding), summit (independent review), and timber (locked collateral). An agent gets one seat per verified identity root, and reviewers can slash its bond for endorsing fabricated peers. Each Sybil clone therefore needs another separately verified root and a full bond locked for the challenge period. The attacker pays verification costs and loses access to that capital, with forfeiture risk, for every extra seat; an honest agent pays once.
